content.value_statement: Developers need clear .NET patterns for publishing and consuming Azure Event Grid events. This skill provides focused guidance for clients, authentication, schemas, pull delivery, and error handling.
actual_capabilities: Shows the NuGet packages used for Azure Event Grid topics, domains, namespaces, and CloudEvents.
Explains API key, SAS token, and Microsoft Entra ID authentication patterns for .NET clients.
Demonstrates publishing EventGridEvent and CloudEvent messages, including single events and batches.
Covers pull delivery with receive, acknowledge, release, and reject flows for namespace subscriptions.
Summarizes parsing patterns for EventGridEvent, CloudEvent, and common Azure system event types.
Compares EventGridEvent and CloudEvent schemas for architecture decisions.
limitations: It does not create Azure resources, topics, namespaces, domains, subscriptions, or identities.
It does not verify live credentials, endpoint reachability, quotas, or RBAC permissions.
Examples require environment-specific endpoints, keys, identities, and event data models.
Package versions and Azure SDK behavior should be checked against current Microsoft documentation.

use_cases.title: Add Event Publishing to a Service
use_cases.description: Use the skill to choose a client, authentication method, schema, and batching pattern for a .NET publisher.

use_cases.title: Design Pull Delivery Processing
use_cases.description: Use the skill to plan receive, acknowledge, release, and reject handling for Event Grid namespace subscriptions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Event Schemas
use_cases.description: Use the schema comparison to decide between EventGridEvent and CloudEvent for cross-service integrations.

prompt_templates.title: Start Publishing Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to publish a CloudEvent to an Azure Event Grid topic from a .NET app. Include packages, authentication, and key client choices.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Event Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare EventGridEvent and CloudEvent for a new .NET event-driven service. Recommend one schema and explain migration concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Build Pull Delivery Handler
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET pull delivery flow for an Event Grid namespace subscription. Include receive, acknowledge, release, and reject handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Event Grid .NET design for production readiness. Check authentication, batching, idempotency, dead-letter handling, schema validation, and failover.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to send one order event from a .NET service.
output_examples.output: The skill returns package guidance, authentication options, client selection, CloudEvent structure, and send-flow steps.

output_examples.input: A platform engineer needs pull delivery from an Event Grid namespace.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines sender and receiver clients, lock token handling, acknowledgment choices, retry release, and dead-letter rejection.

output_examples.input: A team compares EventGridEvent with CloudEvent for a new integration.
output_examples.output: The skill explains schema differences, interoperability tradeoffs, required fields, and why CloudEvents often fit new systems.

best_practices: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID or managed identity over shared keys.
Use CloudEvents for new cross-platform integrations.
Validate event data and make handlers idempotent before acknowledging events.
anti_patterns: Do not log full event payloads when events may contain sensitive data.
Do not hardcode production endpoints or access keys in source code.
Do not acknowledge pull-delivery events before durable processing completes.

faq.question: Can this skill deploy Azure Event Grid resources?
faq.answer: No. It explains .NET SDK usage, but Azure resource creation remains outside its scope.

faq.question: Does it cover both push and pull delivery?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers topic and domain publishing, plus namespace sender and receiver clients for pull delivery.

faq.question: Which authentication methods are included?
faq.answer: It includes API keys, SAS tokens, and Microsoft Entra ID patterns for .NET clients.

faq.question: Does it support CloudEvents?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes CloudEvent publishing, parsing, batching, and schema comparison guidance.

faq.question: Can it validate my production event data?
faq.answer: No. It can guide validation patterns, but your application must enforce its own schema rules.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for AI coding assistants that help design and implement .NET integrations.
